The currently approved powerline corridor for the project will originate from the B.C. Hydro power grid 
in Houston and follow an existing Forest Service Road corridor out to the minesite (see attached map). 
The access route to the mine consists of the following Forest Service Roads:
Road Km.
Morice River 0 - 27
Morice - Owen 27 - 56.5
Morice - Nadina 56.5 - 101
Morice - Tahtsa 101 - 113.6
Huckleberry Connector 113.6 - 122
The construction plans call for the powerline to be located within the existing Forest Service Road right-
of-way as much as is practical. Depending on terrain features and road alignment, the powerline corridor 
may be required to leave the road right-of-way for isolated sections. Poles will normally be set in stable 
ground above the cutslope on the high side of the road a minimum of 3m, and typically 5-7m, from the 
edge of the FSR. This will minimize disturbance outside of the right-of-way, requiring only clearing of 
standing trees within 20-30 m. on either side of the centreline to accommodate the necessary clearing 
boundary. 
The powerline will be constructed primarily of single wood poles, averaging about 15m in height, with 
support bracing as required. Pole spacing will vary with the terrain but will average about 165 m between 
poles. The transmission line itself will be 266.6 mcm Aluminum Conductor Steel Reinforced (ACSR) 
wire, with a diameter of 0.642 inches, energized at 138kV, strung in a wishbone configuration about 
1.5m from the top of the pole. 
For road crossings, the line clearances will be sufficient to ensure that oversize logging trucks or other 
industrial equipment can pass safely beneath the line. These clearances have been determined through 
discussions with the Forest Service and industrial road users.
The existing powerline which runs to Km 13 on the Morice FSR will be re-strung on new poles to avoid 
interference between the two lines. Users will be notified in advance of any interruptions in service. 
Interruptions will be minimized in order to avoid any inconvenience.
The contract for the construction of the powerline has been awarded to McGregor Construction Ltd. of 
Edmonton, Alberta and surveying is being completed by ADW Engineering of Smithers, B.C.

1.  Huckleberry must cause the Project to be designed, located, constructed, operated, dismantled and 
abandoned in accordance with the documents outlined in Schedule “A” to this Project Approval 
Certificate, collectively comprising Huckleberry’s Project Report.

3.  Despite Condition numbers 1 and 2: 
(a) If Huckleberry requires an alternative to the proposed powerline corridor as described in Schedule A, 
Huckleberry must make an application for such alternative to the Executive Director;
(b) The Executive Director, upon receipt of the application for an alternative referred to in Condition 3(a) 
may;
(i) make a recommendation to the Minister and the Minister of Energy, Mines and 
Petroleum Resources as to a review process necessary for an effective assessment of the 
potential effects of the alternative to the proposed powerline corridor, and of whether, 
where the effects are potentially adverse, those effects may be mitigated;
(ii) on approval by the Minister and the Minister of Energy, Mines and Petroleum 
Resources of the proposed review process, establish that review process and cause it to be 
conducted; and
(iii) on conclusion of the review process, make a recommendation to the Minister and the 
Minister of Energy, Mines and Petroleum Resources regarding the alternative powerline 
corridor.
(c) On receipt of the recommendation of the Executive Director, the Minister, with the concurrence of the 
Minister of Energy, Mines and Petroleum Resources, may amend this Project Approval Certificate with 
respect to the alternative powerline corridor.

5. Huckleberry must, in the reasonable opinion of the Minister, have substantially started the Project 
within five years of the issue date of this Project Approval Certificate.

7. Huckleberry must, in good faith, for the life of the Project:
(a) participate in the Huckleberry Mine Aboriginal Liaison Committee (the “HMALC”), 
once it has been established by the province, to address the Aboriginal issues identified in 
the Committee Report, or any other Aboriginal issues that may result from the Project that 
are raised in the HMALC, and recognizing that the HMALC is not intended to be a forum 
for dealing with potential impacts on asserted Aboriginal rights which have already been 
addressed under the environmental assessment process conducted for the Project;
(b) make reasonable efforts to co-operate with other local Aboriginal groups or First 
Nations not on the HMALC whose traditional territories are directly affected by the 
Project, and make attempts to address any concerns resulting from the Project that are 
advanced by any such First Nation or Aboriginal group;

7. Huckleberry must, in good faith, for the life of the Project:
(c) adhere to its First Nations recruitment and placement policy entitled “First Nations 
Recruitment and Placement Policy, Huckleberry Mines Ltd., Huckleberry Project”, dated 
November 10, 1995;

7. Huckleberry must, in good faith, for the life of the Project:
(d) participate in the Huckleberry Technical Acid Rock Drainage Review Committee, once 
it has been established by the province, that will review, monitor and recommend measures 
relevant to Condition 8 of this Project Approval Certificate; and

7. Huckleberry must, in good faith, for the life of the Project:
(e) participate in the “ Morice District Industrial Road Users Group” to address any issues 
identified by, or brought to the attention of, the “Morice District Industrial Road Users 
Group” with respect to the use by Huckleberry of the road access to the Project.

8. If, in the reasonable opinion of the Minister and the Minister of Energy, Mines and Petroleum 
Resources, Huckleberry is not participating in good faith, in the processes referred to in Condition 7, the 
Minister and the Minister of Energy, Mines and Petroleum Resources shall give written notice of further 
measures required of Huckleberry with respect to such participation and within 30 days of receipt of such 
measures, Huckleberry shall implement such measures to the satisfaction of the Minister and the Minister 
of Energy, Mines and Petroleum Resources.

9. Huckleberry, in relation to those activities of the Project that, as set out in section 5.3.1 of the 
Committee Report, with respect to acid rock drainage, are required to be monitored under any approval, 
licence or permit or other authorization issued or given by the appropriate authority pursuant to the Mines 
Act S.B.C. 1989, c.56, s.10, and the Waste Management Act S.B.C. 1982, c. 41, must:
(a) monitor, to the satisfaction of that authority, the effects of such activities;
(b) compare, to the satisfaction of that authority, the anticipated effects of such activities of the Project, 
with the actual effects of such activities of the Project;
(c) evaluate, to the satisfaction of that authority, the adequacy of the measures taken by Huckleberry to 
prevent or mitigate any adverse effects of the activities of the Project; and,
(d) report, in writing to the Executive Director, and to the satisfaction of those authorities referred to 
above in this Condition, the results of such monitoring, comparing and evaluating activities described 
above in Condition 9(a),(b) and (c), as follows:
(i) the first written report to the Executive Director must be delivered by Huckleberry no 
later than March 31 of the year following one full year after the issue date of this Project 
Approval Certificate; and
(ii) subsequent reports must be delivered by Huckleberry to the Executive Director 
annually, by March 31, thereafter during the life of the Project.

10. Huckleberry must:
(a) prepare written reports on the progress of commitments made by Huckleberry at the September 13-
14, 1995 meeting of the Committee, regarding a hiring policy that places preference on hiring residents 
of Northwest, British Columbia and committed to by Huckleberry in a letter dated November 27, 1995, 
and listed in Schedule A to this Project Approval Certificate.
(b) deliver these reports to the Minister, the Minister of Employment and Investment, and the 
Environmental Assessment Office for placement on the project registry, beginning a minimum of one 
month prior to the commencement of construction of the Project and, after that, at six month intervals for 
a period of two years; and
(c) include in these reports, subject to the provisions the Freedom of Information and Protection of 
Privacy Act S.B.C. 1992, c.61, the following matters:
(i) the schedule for construction of the Project,
(ii) the hiring schedule for the Project,
(iii)hiring and employment statistics relating to the Project,
(iv) the steps taken by Huckleberry to support hiring of people resident in the Northwest 
area of British Columbia,
(v) statistics regarding the location of the residences of new employees of Huckleberry,
(vi) the steps taken by Huckleberry to communicate with Aboriginal people regarding 
employment opportunities arising from the Project, and
(vii)statistics on numbers of Aboriginal people employed by Huckleberry.

12. Huckleberry, if so directed by the appropriate authority under an enactment of British Columbia or 
Canada, must comply with any lawful order or direction respecting the road right of way running through 
Felix George Reserve #3 of the Broman Lake Indian Band.

14. Huckleberry shall comply with the requirements of the Fisheries Act (Canada), R.S., 1985, c. F-14, 
and obtain any and all authorizations deemed necessary by the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans.
